headline: Saudi plant maintenance grows at 6.8 per cent as the turnaround becomes a planning discipline
deck: A shutdown is the only time a plant can be opened, and every day of it is production that will not be recovered.
excerpt: With Saudi refining capacity above three million barrels a day and turnarounds on a three-to-five-year cycle, shutdown planning has become a specialist discipline with its own contractors, software and conference circuit.
content:
The turnaround is the single most expensive planned event in a process plant's operating life, and the only opportunity to do the work that cannot be done while running.

The arithmetic is unforgiving. Saudi refining capacity runs above three million barrels a day, and process units are typically turned around every three to five years. During a shutdown the plant produces nothing, so every day is lost margin, and the work is compressed into a window fixed long in advance. The Saudi plant maintenance market has been growing at around 6.8 per cent a year, and the growth is in planning capability as much as in execution labour.

What makes a turnaround difficult is not any individual task but the interaction of thousands of them. Scaffolding has to be built before insulation is stripped, insulation before inspection, inspection before a repair decision, repair before reinstatement, and reinstatement before testing. Each of those is a different trade with a different mobilisation, and the sequence runs across hundreds of equipment items simultaneously.

The worst outcome is a discovery. An inspection finds wall loss that was not anticipated, and a repair that was not in the plan has to be designed, materials procured and welders qualified — inside a window that has no slack. Discovery work is the main reason turnarounds overrun, and reducing it is the main argument for the continuous monitoring that has been displacing periodic inspection. A plant that knows the condition of its equipment before the shutdown can specify the repair scope in advance and procure the materials before the unit comes down.

That is why the integrity discipline and the turnaround discipline have converged. Risk-based inspection decides what gets opened; condition monitoring decides what will be found when it is; and turnaround planning converts both into a schedule that can be resourced. The technical programme at STATIC Arabia in Al Khobar this week runs to more than 240 presentations across 54 sessions, and this cluster of subjects is what most of them address.

The contracting market has been reorganising around the same logic. Integrated operators in the Middle East have been unbundling framework agreements, awarding vibration monitoring and corrosion analytics to digital specialists while retaining mechanical execution with established turnaround contractors, and separating condition-based monitoring from catalyst handling and vessel inspection scopes.

For contractors, the implication is that mobilisation capability alone is no longer the differentiator it was. For operators, the implication is a more complex vendor map, with the analysis and the wrench work bought from different suppliers and the integration risk retained in house.

STOT Saudi, the Kingdom's dedicated shutdown, turnaround and maintenance event, follows later this month in Jubail Industrial City from 28 to 30 September.
author: Mo Qureshi
scheduledReason: Written before the relevant day of STATIC Arabia, which runs 8-10 September at Dhahran Expo. It works from the published programme and independently verified industry data, and reports nothing from the event.
